request: 解析一下《黄色墙纸》这篇小说。

sources.title: The Yellow Wallpaper
sources.read_scope: Entire story continuously read, web lines 24–485 across initial open and overlapping final open; license excluded.

sources.title: Why I wrote The Yellow Wallpaper?
sources.read_scope: Complete author statement lines 461–475; Cambridge reprint metadata.

story.statement: Rest cure restricts work; secret journal gives way to wallpaper study; woman becomes rescue project; locked-room tearing culminates in crawling over fainted husband.

characters.statement: John's affectionate actions coexist with rejecting her account and choices; absence of deliberate cruelty does not remove coercive effects.
Jennie upholds domestic competence; narrator feels inadequate as wife and mother.

tone.statement: Early humor and self-correction shift toward grotesque sensory immersion; narrator's excitement diverges from reader alarm.

ideas.statement: Authority to interpret distress becomes a central conflict; her mental deterioration does not invalidate every observation.
Check against simple emancipation: she refuses exit, uses rope, and circles room.

highlights.statement: Secret interrupted writing makes suppression part of narrative form; wallpaper evolves from object to private task and substitute world.
Existing wall damage is retrospectively unsettled by biting bed and shoulder matching smooch, without establishing previous inmates.

ending.statement: Crawling over John reverses posture and authority while room-bound repetition prevents uncomplicated victory.

context.statement: Author reports rest cure restrictions and recovery through work, distinguishes fictional hallucinations from own experience.

essay_plan.throughline: Follow the loss of recognized voice into secret study, rescue, identification and ambivalent final reversal.
sections: Develop John and Jennie through concrete interactions
Explain narrative voice and tonal divergence
Read final actions and qualify freedom
Use author statement and return to secrecy
essay_plan.context_reception_decision: Include author statement because it clarifies rest cure and fiction/autobiography distinction. Omit broad reception history: not needed for this reading; author-reported treatment changes not independently verified.

open_questions: Final Jane reference does not securely identify narrator; omitted from explanation rather than asserting a name.
